basis_seams.declared: config/valuation_sets/prospx_current.yaml meta.win_cost_basis: 'FA-signings-implied $/WAR (data/fa_dpw_series.json, trailing 3-winter mean)'; params.win_cost.disable_fa_implied: false with the comment 'production leaves the FA-implied rescale ON'.
basis_seams.actual: Production runs valuation_sets.DEFAULT_SET = clemens_2026, whose params.win_cost.disable_fa_implied is TRUE. Live value_framework._config()['dollars_per_war'] = flat 11.74M, fa_implied {'enabled': False}. So the FA-implied rescale is OFF.
basis_seams.numeric_divergence_today: prospect surplus and /trademachine/ vet surplus price a win at $11.7400M flat (value_framework.tiered_war_value_usd, unrescaled - verified in mlb_trade_lookup._compute_surplus). /projections/ RESCALES the identical value_framework tiered value by (winter_dpw / base_flat): proj_export._season_value_usd:128. Measured live: winter_dpw(2026) = $14,701,738 vs base_flat $11,740,000, ratio 1.2523. THE SAME 3.0-WAR SEASON IS WORTH $51.21M ON /projections/ AND $40.89M ON /trademachine/, a +25.2% gap (+20.8% for the 2027 winter). /fa/ prices on the same FA-implied series. Both models are registered 'validated'. Separately, the trailing-3-winter mean of data/fa_dpw_series.json is $13.0252M (+10.95% over base_flat) and the 2026 realized winter is $13.5826M (+15.70%).
basis_seams.severity: high - post-ETA prospects are served on BOTH /projections/ and /trademachine/ (registry: mlb_projections_prospects, trade_machine_surplus), so one player carries two dollar values 25% apart, and the yaml comment asserts the opposite of production.

basis_seams.declared: efv_board_side_scale shipped 2026-07-25 on the owner directive 'by the Clemens framework, hitter/pitcher FVs translate to different outcomes'; it raises pitcher grades (top-25 pitcher share 0.04 -> 0.12).
basis_seams.actual: value_framework.realized_implied_fv ACCEPTS is_pitcher and IGNORES it (measured: identical FV for hit and pit at 2/4/6/9/12/16/20 WAR, max delta 0.02 = rounding). So xfv_grade is a pure WAR-implied quantity: two players at the same grade have, by construction, the same E[6yr WAR]. value_framework.surplus_value_mm then prices the pitcher at 0.500x (FV40) to 0.862x (FV70) of the hitter at the SAME grade. In config/valuation_sets/prospx_current.yaml the ctrl_war column is BYTE-IDENTICAL for hitter and pitcher at every tier (1.14 ... 15.12) while surplus_musd is not (FV60: 78.6 vs 63.8).
basis_seams.numeric_divergence_today: same grade, same modelled control WAR, 19.0% less money at FV60 and 50.0% less at FV40, purely for being a pitcher.
basis_seams.severity: high (coherence, not necessarily accuracy). The pitcher haircut may be a correct risk/durability price, but it is applied at the DOLLAR layer to a grade whose WAR content is already role-equalised, while a same-day ship moves the grade the OTHER way. Nothing in either model's notes reconciles the two. Needs one owner and one written basis.
